before: ESM protein representations showed modest correspondence with PPI topology. Directly connected protein pairs had a mean cosine similarity of 0.8789, compared with 0.8639 for randomly paired proteins; within-community similarity also exceeded between-community similarity (Fig. 3A). Performance differences between fixed PPI-GCN propagation and raw ESM varied non-monotonically across network strata. For example, mid-k-core variants showed a $\Delta$AUC of +0.0775, whereas high-degree variants showed $-$0.0178 (Fig. 3B). Betweenness, clustering and neighbour-risk strata also exhibited heterogeneous performance differences (Fig. 3C,D).
after: ESM protein representations showed modest correspondence with PPI topology. Directly connected protein pairs had a mean cosine similarity of 0.8789, compared with 0.8639 for randomly paired proteins; within-community similarity also exceeded between-community similarity (Fig. 3A). Performance differences between full FPP and raw ESM varied non-monotonically across network strata using three-seed ensemble probabilities. For example, mid-k-core variants showed a $\Delta$AUC of +0.0603, whereas high-degree variants showed $-$0.0216 (Fig. 3B). Betweenness, clustering and neighbour-risk strata also exhibited heterogeneous performance differences (Fig. 3C,D).

before: Among 53 joint topology cells examined on the same test set, we observed both positive and negative performance differences, including mid-k-core/high-betweenness ($\Delta$AUC +0.1429) and high-k-core/low-clustering ($\Delta$AUC $-$0.0532; Fig. 3E,F). Because the highlighted cells were selected after examining the test-set results and their intervals were computed using variant-level resampling, these estimates do not account for within-protein dependence or subgroup-selection uncertainty. We therefore interpret these patterns as exploratory findings that require independent validation.
after: Among 53 joint topology cells examined on the same test set, we observed both positive and negative performance differences, including mid-k-core/high-betweenness ($\Delta$AUC +0.1115) and high-k-core/low-clustering ($\Delta$AUC $-$0.0486; Fig. 3E,F). The four highlighted cells were selected using reference-model predictions on the same test set and fixed before the ensemble analysis. Paired protein-clustered 95\% intervals included zero in three of these four cells. The intervals account for repeated variants within proteins but condition on fitted models and the graph; they do not account for post-hoc subgroup selection or multiple comparisons. We therefore interpret these patterns as exploratory findings that require independent validation.
